note: Session 14: Route context bleeding fix — agent_service clears LLM-inferred route_id when current message has new origin/location but no route number; extract_origin_place() regex hardened with word boundaries (\b); 12 new tests, 157 total all green. vision.statement: An AI-powered transit assistant for Gainesville RTS riders that understands plain-language questions and guides the customer to the right answer — whether that's a real-time ETA or a scheduled departure time.
vision.cx_journey: Customer arrives at the assistant and types a question in plain language (e.g. 'When does the next 75 leave Butler Plaza?'). The assistant leads the interaction — asking clarifying questions when needed — until it can deliver the specific ETA or schedule information the rider needs.
vision.wizard_strategy: The Trip Wizard is the conversation flow prototype. It makes the decision tree explicit (intent → route → stop → direction → result) in a structured UI so the paths can be validated. Once proven, the same guided logic is translated into the chat assistant's prompting — the AI replicates the wizard's flow in natural language instead of button clicks.
vision.end_state: A single assistant interface where any RTS rider can ask a transit question in plain English (or Spanish) and get a reliable, accurate answer without needing to know stop IDs, route numbers, or schedules.

tasks.title: P1-A: Label real-time vs static schedule in every response
tasks.details: Research finding: users trained by Google Maps expect all answers to be real-time. When we return a GTFS schedule time they treat it as an ETA — trust collapses when bus doesn't match. Fix: prefix real-time responses with 'Live tracker shows...' and schedule responses with 'Scheduled at X (static schedule)'. Use existing sources metadata (source_type: realtime vs backend_basics_schedule) to drive the label automatically in response_builder.py.

tasks.title: P1-B: Add human escalation after 2-3 consecutive failures
tasks.details: Research finding: 2–3 failed disambiguations is the universal chatbot abandonment threshold (CTA study, WorkBot analysis). After 2–3 'need_stop_or_route' / 'clarify_route_vs_stop' responses in a session, append 'Still stuck? Call RTS Customer Service: (352) 334-2600 or visit go-rts.com'. Implementation: session_manager tracks failure_count per session; agent_service checks it and appends escalation note. Equity requirement — elderly and low-literacy riders have no recourse without this.

tasks.title: P1-C: Confirm fuzzy stop matches before using them
tasks.details: When _gtfs_resolve_stop_name() matches via fuzzy/token search (not exact or stop_id direct), we currently respond with full confidence. If the match is wrong, user gets wrong stop schedule. Fix: add match_type field ('exact', 'fuzzy') to _gtfs_resolve_stop_name() and resolve_stop_global() results. In agent_service.py, when match_type='fuzzy', ask for confirmation: 'I think you mean Stop 0473 – Reitz Union. Is that right? [Yes] [Different stop]' before fetching predictions.

tasks.title: P2-D: Landmark-to-stop resolution for arbitrary locations

Users say 'near Walmart on Archer Road' or 'the stop by Publix on University Ave' — not GTFS stop names. stop_areas.json covers zones (UF, Downtown) but not arbitrary landmarks. Options: (A) Expand stop_areas.json with known Gainesville landmarks mapped to specific stop IDs — low cost, limited coverage. (B) Add Google Places / OSM geocoding call to find nearest GTFS stop to a described location — broader coverage, adds external API dependency. Start with option A (curated landmark map), document gap for option B.

tasks.title: P2-F: Enforce brevity in HUMANIZE_ENABLED responses

tasks.title: Tool-Use Refactor: Design tool schema (inputs, outputs, status codes)
tasks.details: Define the 5 tools the LLM will call instead of the current rule-code pipeline. Each tool must return an explicit status field — never empty arrays. Tools: (1) search_stops(name_or_landmark) → [{stop_id, stop_name, match_type}] or {status: 'no_match'}. (2) get_realtime_predictions(stop_id) → [{route, minutes, headsign}] or {status: 'no_service' | 'api_unavailable'}. (3) query_schedule(route_id, stop_id_or_name, time?, date?) → [{departure, headsign}] or {status: 'no_trips' | 'stop_not_found' | 'route_not_found'}. (4) get_routes_at_stop(stop_id) → [{route_id, headsign}]. (5) get_route_overview(route_id, date?) → {first, last, frequency_min, directions[]} or {status: 'no_service'}. Document inputs/outputs/status codes before writing any code.

tasks.title: Tool-Use Refactor: Implement tool wrapper functions
tasks.details: Create routes/agent_tools.py. Wrap existing services as clean tool-callable functions matching the schema from tooluse-1. Each wrapper: (1) calls the existing service (schedule_service, rts_api, stop_resolver) — no new business logic. (2) Always returns an explicit status so the LLM never sees ambiguous empty results. (3) Handles exceptions internally and returns {status: 'error', message: ...} rather than raising. Keep all existing service code untouched — this is just a translation layer. Depends on: tooluse-1.

tasks.title: Tool-Use Refactor: Write the system prompt with grounding rules
tasks.details: Write the system prompt that defines what the LLM is, what it can do, and what it must never do. Must include: (1) Persona: RTS Gainesville transit assistant. (2) Hard grounding rule: ONLY state departure times and stop names that appear in a tool result from this conversation. Never use training knowledge about bus schedules. (3) No-hallucination rule: if a tool returns no results or an error, say exactly that — do not guess or interpolate. (4) Tool-call-first rule: always call a tool before answering any factual transit question. (5) Language rule: respond in the language the user wrote in (EN/ES). (6) Brevity rule: 3 sentences max, preserve times/routes/stop IDs exactly. Can be written in parallel with tooluse-2.

tasks.title: Tool-Use Refactor: Build the tool-use agent orchestration loop
tasks.details: Create routes/agent_v2.py with a single handle_message(msg, history, session_ctx) function. Pattern: (1) Build messages array from history. (2) Call LLM with tools defined. (3) If response has tool_calls: execute each tool, append results to messages, call LLM again. (4) Repeat until no tool_calls (max 5 iterations to prevent loops). (5) Return final text answer + any button suggestions the LLM emits. LLM choice: gpt-4o-mini (already integrated, existing _openai_client() helper reused). Temperature = 0 for all tool-synthesis responses. Depends on: tooluse-2 and tooluse-3.

tasks.title: Tool-Use Refactor: Wire new agent into Flask API
tasks.details: Add /api/agent/v2 POST endpoint in agent_api.py pointing to agent_v2.handle_message(). Keep /api/agent (old pipeline) running in parallel for fallback. Frontend chat.html gets a temporary toggle (ENV var AGENT_VERSION=v2) to switch which endpoint sendAgentMessage() calls. Once v2 is validated, swap /api/agent to point to the new loop and remove the old pipeline. SSE streaming endpoint /api/agent/stream should also support v2 path. Depends on: tooluse-4.

tasks.title: Tool-Use Refactor: Test all key conversation scenarios
tasks.details: Run and document these specific scenarios before declaring v2 ready: (1) 'Next bus at Rosa Parks' → ETA list (no route specified). (2) 'What about from Santa Fe college?' (follow-up, route must NOT bleed). (3) 'What routes go to UF?' → route discovery. (4) 'Route 43 schedule tomorrow morning' → first/last with frequency. (5) 'First bus after 5pm on route 43 from downtown' → schedule, not first-of-day. (6) 'The one after that?' → advance past last shown departure. (7) Spanish: '¿Cuándo viene el próximo bus?' → responde en español. (8) Unknown landmark: 'Bus near Walmart on Archer' → graceful no-match or best effort. Each scenario: record exact input/output, mark pass/fail. Depends on: tooluse-5.

tasks.title: Tool-Use Refactor: Deploy to Render and validate in production
tasks.details: Push to Render with AGENT_VERSION=v2 env var. Run smoke tests: health endpoint, 3 ETA queries at known stops, 1 schedule query, 1 route discovery, 1 Spanish query. Confirm no hallucinated times in any response. Monitor Render logs for tool call errors or LLM loop termination warnings. Once stable for 24h: flip default to v2, remove old pipeline in a cleanup commit. Update MEMORY.md and project_tasks.json. Depends on: tooluse-6.
